title: Challenge 25 & Age-Restricted Sales
blurb: When to ask for ID, which ID to accept, spotting proxy sales and handling a refusal.
siteNotes: The venue's written age verification policy and the refusals log: where it is kept and how to fill it in.
Which managers to call on each shift when someone pushes back after a refusal.
Whether the venue accepts any other ID beyond photo driving licence, passport and PASS-hologram cards.
legalNotes: Selling alcohol to anyone under 18 is an offence: Licensing Act 2003, s.146. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2003/17

Premises licences carry a mandatory condition that an age verification policy operates (Challenge 21 or Challenge 25 are the usual forms): Licensing Act 2003 (Mandatory Licensing Conditions) Order 2010, as amended.
Buying alcohol for someone under 18 on licensed premises is also an offence (proxy sales): Licensing Act 2003, s.149.

CHECK: the trainer says "the person who makes the sale can be personally fined". This is right, but the law does not set a fixed small fine; please confirm you are happy with the wording used on the slides.

CHECK: the trainer lists photo driving licence, passport and PASS hologram card as valid ID. Some premises also accept military ID or approved digital ID; confirm the venue's policy and update if needed.
CHECK: the refusals log is good practice and usually part of the venue's age verification policy rather than a direct legal requirement; confirm.

cards.title: Challenge 25 & Age-Restricted Sales
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- ask for ID whenever someone looks under 25
- tell valid ID from invalid ID
- refuse politely and record every refusal

cards.title: It is on you as well as the business
cards.body:
Selling alcohol is a privilege that comes with real responsibility. It is a criminal offence to sell alcohol to anyone under 18.

It is not just the business that is on the line. The person who makes the sale can be personally fined, and a personal licence holder can lose their licence.

left.title: At risk
items: The person who made the sale

right.title: Not at risk
items: Nobody: it is never only the business

cards.title: If they look under 25, ask
cards.body:
If a customer looks under 25, you ask for ID before serving them alcohol. Someone who is genuinely 18 will not mind proving it, and it gives you a comfortable margin.

If they cannot prove they are 18 or over, you politely refuse.

> No ID, no sale.

items.title: Looks under 25?
items.text: Ask for ID before serving alcohol.

items.title: Cannot prove it?
items.text: Politely refuse. No ID, no sale.

cards.title: Only accept valid photo ID
cards.body:
Accept a photo driving licence, a passport, or a card carrying the PASS hologram.

Check the photo really is them, check the date of birth, and make sure the ID looks genuine and has not been tampered with.

cards.title: Watch for proxy sales
cards.body: A proxy sale is an adult buying alcohol to pass to an under-18. If you spot it, refuse the sale.

left.title: Check
items: The ID looks genuine and untampered

right.title: Refuse
items: Proxy sale: adult buying for an under-18

cards.title: Record it, and call a manager
cards.body:
Every time you refuse a sale, record it in the refusals log. It protects you and shows we take our licence seriously.

If a customer gets pushy after a refusal, do not feel you have to back down or handle it alone: call a manager. When you are unsure about someone's age, the safe answer is to ask for ID, or ask a manager.

items.title: Record
items.text: Write it in the refusals log.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Looks under 25? Ask for ID. No ID, no sale
- Valid ID: photo driving licence, passport or PASS hologram card
- Check the photo, the date of birth and that it is genuine
- Refuse proxy sales, record every refusal and call a manager if pushed

cards.q: Under Challenge 25, you ask for ID if a customer looks under...
cards.why: Challenge 25 means asking for ID from anyone who looks under 25, which gives a comfortable margin over 18.

cards.q: Selling alcohol to someone under 18 is a criminal offence.
cards.why: It is a criminal offence to sell alcohol to anyone under 18.

cards.q: If a customer cannot prove they are 18 or over, what should you do?
cards.why: No ID, no sale. Refuse politely.

cards.q: Which of these is valid ID?
cards.why: Only a photo driving licence, a passport or a card with the PASS hologram is accepted.

cards.q: A card with a PASS hologram is acceptable ID.
cards.why: A card carrying the PASS hologram is one of the accepted forms of ID.

options: A sale rung through by a trainee
A sale made to a regular guest
An adult buying alcohol for an under-18
A sale put on to a room account
cards.why: In a proxy sale an adult buys alcohol to pass to an under-18. If you spot it, refuse the sale.

cards.q: You should record every refused sale in the refusals log.
cards.why: Every refusal goes in the log. It protects you and shows we take our licence seriously.

cards.q: On an ID you should check the photo, that it is genuine, and the...
cards.why: Check the photo is them, the date of birth, and that the ID looks genuine and has not been tampered with.

cards.q: Only the business is at risk if alcohol is sold to a minor, never the individual server.
cards.why: The person who makes the sale can be personally fined, and a personal licence holder can lose their licence.

cards.q: A customer becomes pushy after you refuse. What's a sensible next step?
options: Give in to keep the peace
Serve them at the next till
cards.why: Do not back down and do not handle it alone. Call a manager.
